lines.text: Alien Invasion. Signal Decoders.
Chapter one. The First Signal.
December the twenty-fifth. Twenty thirty-two.
London has fallen.
A colossal attack fell on this once great city.
It erased every signal, every screen, every voice that once connected the city.
Power grids collapsed in seconds.
Satellites fell from the sky.
Communication, eradicated. And the people... lost.
The city went dark.
On Christmas night, above the rooftops, a strange, luminous ripple hums through the clouds.
Too low to hear. Too powerful to ignore.
And beneath the streets, in forgotten tunnels and abandoned stations, the last survivors wait in the dark.
They call themselves...
The Decoders.
Are you ready to join them, and help decode the signal? Say yes, or no.
Are you ready to join the Decoders? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Are you ready to join the Decoders? Say yes, or no.
The Decoders can't do this alone. They need someone with sharp ears, and a brave heart.
Will you help them? Say yes, or no.
Will you help the Decoders? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Will you help the Decoders? Say yes, or no.
That's okay, Decoder. The radio will be waiting for you.
I swear my legs are going to detach from my body.
That would be efficient. At least one of us would escape!
Do you always have to be so sarcastic? All the...
Did you hear that?
Hear what?
THAT! RIGHT THERE!
Oh. That's just static.
Robin... it's STATIC!
Yeah. Just static.
Robin!
Oh my gosh, yes! STATIC!
Ha ha! Yes!
Ha ha!
Where is it?
It's somewhere here!
No, here! Over here!
There! Under the debris!
Alex, watch out! The debris is more unstable than your posture!
An old handheld radio... that's what survived the pulse?
Nothing has worked since the pulse. NOTHING! Not even military gear!
It's analog. That's why it survived.
Oh!
Nothing but noise.
Try adjusting the frequency?
Hold on, hold on! That doesn't sound random...
It almost sounds like music.
High. Low. High.
That's deliberate.
You think it's a message?
Or it could be something else...
Like what?
The music is not just noise. It is a message... the only way the Decoders will get to the truth.
And now... you are part of the team.
Welcome, Decoder.
Your job is to help Alex and Robin interpret the signal. Spot patterns. Solve puzzles. Stay alive.
The radio is playing three repeating tones.
High.
Low.
High.
Robin believes the tones match musical notes.
If High equals the note C, and Low equals the note A... what three-letter pattern is the signal playing?
Say your answer out loud.
If High is the note C, and Low is the note A, what three letters is the signal playing? High, Low, High.
Hmm. Not quite. Listen again.
High is C. Low is A. So High... Low... High... spells what?
If High is C, and Low is A, what three letters is the signal playing? High, Low, High.
Listen carefully.
If High is C, and Low is A, what three letters is the signal playing?
If High is the note C, and Low is the note A, what three letters is the signal playing? High, Low, High.
Wait, wait, I've got it! High is C, and Low is A... so it's C, A, C!
Yes! C, A, C. That is it!
So the signal is a spelling?
Alex! Dude! ALEX! Someone is out there sending a signal, hoping for us to GET IT! We're not alone, buddy!
Yes! So we... we keep this radio working! Somehow, every day. Wait for it... wait for the signal.
Yes. C. A. C. That's the pattern.
So... it's spelling? A word?
It's structured. Which means it was built to be understood.
That means someone out there is trying to talk to us!
Or trying to see who's still alive.
Why would they do that? Why not just hit us with another pulse?
I don't know! Maybe this is a trap!
You always go straight to the worst version.
Because the worst version keeps you breathing!
Dude! We're not alone! After days... there's finally something else! That has to mean something good, man!
I don't know, dude...
Then we keep listening. We learn it. Every day.
And what if listening is exactly what it wants?
What if NOT listening gets us caught faster?
Look, man. I don't know what's at the other end of this. But all we can do is keep going!
Fine.
We keep the radio alive. But we don't answer back. Not yet.
Deal.
The radio hisses softly in the dark. Decoder, should they keep listening tonight? Say yes, or no.
Should Alex and Robin keep listening to the radio tonight? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Should Alex and Robin keep listening to the radio tonight? Say yes, or no.
Fine. I'll switch it off. Just for tonight.
Robin, wait. Listen!
The frequency just spiked.
That sound... that's the sky.
No. It's coming from everywhere.
It's getting louder...
It's matching the pulse pattern.
The one that SHUT DOWN THE WHOLE CITY?!
Robin! Robin! This is the sound from that night! From Christmas!
It's similar. But not identical.
What do you mean?!
Something is trying to copy it.
WHAT? How do you know? And when did you become an expert?!
Because we're still awake! We haven't passed out like last time!
Dude! If the ground keeps shaking like this, we might just pass out!
Just hold on!
The sound fades. And the city is just as it was, mere seconds ago.
This time, it does not destroy them. It does not silence them.
So what changed? And what does it mean, when the sound that ended the world... no longer can?
Decoder, what do you think? Is the signal trying to help them? Say yes, or no.
Do you think the signal is trying to help Alex and Robin? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Do you think the signal is trying to help Alex and Robin? Say yes, or no.
Me too, Decoder! Something out there is looking out for us.
I'm with you, Decoder. Something about this doesn't add up.
The sound is gone. But the question remains.
Why did the signal not destroy them like before? Why did it fade, instead of finishing what it started?
Two days pass in silence. No hum. No tones. No answers.
Only the radio... waiting.
It's back!
It's back!
Okay, okay! Let's listen now!
The music returns. Changed. Careful. As if it is trying again... differently.
And now... you are part of the team.
Welcome back, Decoder. Your job is to help Alex and Robin interpret the signal. Spot patterns. Solve puzzles. Stay alive.
It's using the same notes as before.
So... C, C, C, C. A, A. C, C. A. C.
But it's not making any sense! This is not a word!
Maybe it's a pattern!
If High equals C, and Low equals A... the signal is no longer asking what the notes are... but how many of them there are.
What does the new signal mean? Count each group of notes, and say the numbers out loud.
Count the notes in each group of the signal. What numbers do you hear?
Hmm, not quite. Let's count each group together.
The first group has four high notes. So that's four. How many notes are in each group after that?
Count the notes in each group. The first group has four. What numbers come next?
Listen again, and count each group.
How many notes are in each group?
Count the notes in each group of the signal. What numbers do you hear?
Let me count. Four highs... two lows... two highs... one low... and one high. Four, two, two, one, one!
Four. Two. Two. One. One.
So it stopped spelling... and started counting?
It added another layer.
It's not a layer... maybe it's a code!
Okay, great! What do we do with this... code?
I don't know...
C, A, C... and four, two, two, one, one.
Look, I know it doesn't make any sense. But we need to keep solving the codes, the music, until it does!
Well, whatever this is, we can at least confirm it isn't something random!
So let's assume the signal is guiding us.
Or watching us.
We didn't send anything back.
No. But we heard it!
That doesn't mean it knows we exist.
It changed when we understood it.
Maybe we're picking up a message that's meant for someone else?
Oh, great! Now we're eavesdropping!
Think about it! If this were the Choir, wouldn't they just attack, or drag us out of here?
I don't even want to think that it's the Choir!
How can you be scared to THINK?
Because in the span of minutes, they wiped out an ENTIRE CITY! Are you forgetting who the Choir are?
They're not a band. They're an alien sentinel, from somewhere beyond! They didn't come with ships or soldiers. They came with one frequency.
One sound shut down everything. Power grids. Satellites. People.
The radio crackles.
The pattern fractures into static. A distorted voice slips through the noise.
Not... alone...
Did it just... speak?
Umm...
But we didn't speak.
We listened.
How does it know?
The Decoders must decide their next move.
Option one. Follow the signal toward its source.
Option two. Shut down the radio, and remain hidden underground.
Say follow, or hide.
Should the Decoders follow the signal, or hide? Say follow, or hide.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Should the Decoders follow the signal, or hide? Say follow, or hide.
Whoever that was...
It may, or may not, know that we're here.
Maybe there's a way... we can make them know... about us?
No! That's WAY too risky!
Then what do you suggest we do...
You chose to follow the signal.
This is only the beginning. Your choice will shape what happens next.
End of chapter one.
You chose to stay hidden. The radio falls silent... for now.
This is only the beginning. Your choice will shape what happens next.
End of chapter one.
Alien Invasion. Signal Decoders.
Chapter two. The Map in the Music.
Previously... a strange signal crackled out of an old radio. It spelled C, A, C. Then it counted: four, two, two, one, one.
And then, a voice slipped through the static...
Not... alone...
Right! We said we'd follow the signal. So... where is it actually coming from?
Oh, sure. Let me just check the giant glowing arrow in the sky.
For two nights, the Decoders kept the radio switched off. But on the third night...
It switched itself on. Alex... it switched itself ON.
Then it really, really wants us to listen.
Four, two, two, one, one. Again!
It keeps playing the same numbers. It's like a song that's stuck.
Unless... they're not just numbers. What if they're... turns?
Turns?
Like directions! Four junctions, then two, then two...
The old maintenance tunnels! They're full of junctions! If you count them...
...the music is a map! Grab the radio!
The Decoders creep deeper into the tunnels than they have ever dared to go.
Junction four, two, two, one, one. This is where the counting stops.
So which way now?
Four notes this time. High, low, low, high.
Directions! What if High means left... and Low means right?
Decoder, the tunnels split again and again. The signal plays four notes.
If High means left, and Low means right... which four ways should they turn? Say the four turns out loud.
If High means left, and Low means right, which four ways should they turn?
Hmm, not quite. The first note is High... so the first turn is left. Listen again.
High means left. Low means right. What are the four turns?
If High means left, and Low means right, which four ways should they turn?
Listen carefully.
If High means left, and Low means right, which four ways do they turn?
If High means left, and Low means right, which four ways should they turn?
Wait, I've got it! High, left. Low, right. Low, right. High, left! Left, right, right, left!
Left, right, right, left. That's it!
Left. Right. Right. Left. The tunnels twist and turn... until they end at a heavy green door.
Hello? Is anybody in there?
Who's there? If you're from Halcyon, you can turn RIGHT back around!
Halcyon? The satellite company?
We're not Halcyon! We're... Decoders! We followed the music!
Anyone can say that. Prove it.
What did the signal spell... the very first time?
Decoder, do you remember? High was C, and Low was A.
What did the signal spell, the very first time? Say the three letters.
What three letters did the signal spell, the very first time?
Think back! High was C, and Low was A. Listen.
High, Low, High spells what?
What three letters did the signal spell, the very first time?
Listen again.
High is C, and Low is A. What did the signal spell?
What three letters did the signal spell, the very first time?
C, A, C! It spelled C, A, C!
C, A, C. You really did hear it.
Sorry about that. You can't be too careful. Halcyon drones have been sniffing around these tunnels for weeks.
Whoa. Is this... a radio studio?
An old emergency broadcast room. Built so somebody could talk to all of London, if everything else failed.
Well. Everything else failed. I'm Ada.
Robin. And this is Alex. He gets excited about rocks.
That was ONE rock. And it was shaped like a duck!
Ada... what's that writing on the wall?
The Choir is not the enemy. It was already here when I found this place. I don't know who wrote it.
Not the enemy? The Choir shut down the whole city!
That's what everyone says. But I used to build antennas for Halcyon, the company that ran London's satellites. And some things... never added up.
Ada knows things about Halcyon. But can she be trusted? Decoder, should they trust Ada? Say yes, or no.
Should Alex and Robin trust Ada? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Should Alex and Robin trust Ada? Say yes, or no.
I trust her! She has a secret radio room. Secret radio room people are always good.
I'll take that.
I'm with you, Decoder. We keep one eye on her.
That's... fair. I'd do exactly the same.
Citizens of London. This is Director Sterling, of Halcyon.
The Choir still hunts above. Stay underground. Stay quiet. And do not, under any circumstances, listen to strange signals.
Halcyon will keep you safe.
Sterling. My old boss.
Wait. Why is a satellite company telling everyone what to do?
That... is exactly the right question.
And why doesn't he want anybody listening to signals?
Somewhere above the tunnels, a secret is waiting to be decoded.
End of chapter two.

end.title: Chapter 2: The Map in the Music

lines.text: Alien Invasion. Signal Decoders.
Chapter three. Halcyon.
Previously... the Decoders followed the map in the music to a secret radio room, and met Ada, who used to work for Halcyon.
On the wall, someone had written: the Choir is not the enemy. And then, Director Sterling's voice came over the speakers.
Okay. Let me show you something.
This is the Lattice. Four hundred Halcyon satellites, all the way around the Earth.
Sterling used to brag that the Lattice could talk to every single phone in London... all at the same time.
One sound... shut down everything.
Wait. What if the pulse didn't come from the Choir? What if it came from... the Lattice?
That's what I've been too scared to say out loud.
If there's any proof, it'll be in the Halcyon depot. Under the old power station, by the river.
Of course it's under a power station. It's never under a nice bakery.
After a long, dark walk, they reach a giant steel door.
A keypad lock. It needs a three-number code.
Can you hack it?
Hack it? I can LISTEN to it. Every number makes the lock beep.
Shh! Listen!
Decoder, the lock beeps in three groups.
Count the beeps in each group, and say the three numbers.
Count the beeps in each group. What are the three numbers?
Not quite! The first group has three beeps, so the first number is three. Listen again.
How many beeps are in the other two groups?
Count the beeps in each group. What are the three numbers?
Listen again.
Count the beeps in each group. What are the three numbers?
Count the beeps in each group. What are the three numbers?
Three beeps... one beep... four beeps. Three, one, four!
Three, one, four. We're in!
Whoa. This place is HUGE.
And full of satellites. Why does a satellite company need a secret basement?
Drone! A Halcyon security drone!
The drone's red searchlight sweeps closer. Decoder, should they hide behind the crates? Say yes, or no.
Should they hide behind the crates? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Should they hide behind the crates? Say yes, or no.
They dive behind the crates. The searchlight slides over their heads... and moves on.
They freeze, as still as statues. The red light sweeps right across Robin's boots...
Don't. Sneeze.
...and the drone floats away.
That was close.
Over here! A Halcyon terminal!
It's locked. It wants a password...
Listen! It's beeping. Short, short, short. Long, long, long. Short, short, short.
That's Morse code!
Decoder, this is Morse code. Three short beeps make the letter S. Three long beeps make the letter O.
What three letters is the terminal asking for? Say them out loud.
Three short beeps are S. Three long beeps are O. What three letters is it asking for?
Not quite! Short, short, short is S. Long, long, long is O. Listen again.
What three letters is that?
Three short beeps are S. Three long beeps are O. What three letters is it asking for?
Listen again.
Three short beeps are S. Three long beeps are O. What three letters is it asking for?
Three short beeps are S. Three long beeps are O. What three letters is it asking for?
S... O... S! It's S, O, S! The signal for help!
S, O, S! Of course. The emergency code.
On the screen, a secret file opens. Its name... Project Hush.
Project Hush. Log one. On Christmas night, the Lattice will sing a single note.
Every phone, every screen, every radio will go silent. London will go quiet.
And when the people wake up, frightened and confused... we'll tell them it was the sky.
And they will need Halcyon more than ever.
He did it. Sterling made the pulse.
And he blamed the Choir!
So the Choir... was never the enemy.
The drone! It's seen us!
RUN!
Can the Decoders escape Halcyon... and tell the world the truth?
End of chapter three.
Alien Invasion. Signal Decoders.
Chapter four. The Choir.
Previously... deep in the Halcyon depot, the Decoders uncovered Project Hush. Director Sterling made the pulse himself, and blamed the sky.
And then, a Halcyon drone spotted them...
Up and up they run, out of the tunnels, until cold air hits their faces.
We're... outside! We haven't been outside since Christmas!
Out in the open. Not my favourite place.
Guys. Look. Up.
Above the river, the clouds begin to glow.
It's the Choir. It's the CHOIR!
Not... alone...
It's... singing. It's singing our music!
Alex. Robin. There's something I need to tell you.
The signal. The music on your radio... I've been passing it on. Every night, from my antenna.
YOU sent it?
Not exactly. The song isn't mine. It's the Choir's. I just... made it loud enough for people to hear.
So the signal comes from the Choir... and you!
Halcyon hunts anyone who sends signals. I was scared. I'm sorry.
Ada, you ran a secret pirate radio station for aliens. That's the coolest thing anyone has ever done.
Really?
Above them, the Choir sings again. The same notes as before... but the other way round.
Decoder, the Choir is singing the old code backwards.
The code was four, two, two, one, one. What are those numbers backwards? Say the five numbers.
The code was four, two, two, one, one. What is it backwards?
Not quite! Start at the end. Four, two, two, one, ONE. So backwards, it starts with one, one...
What are all five numbers backwards?
The code was four, two, two, one, one. What is it backwards?
Listen again.
The code was four, two, two, one, one. What is it backwards?
The code was four, two, two, one, one. What is it backwards?
One, one, two, two, four! It's our code backwards!
Backwards! Of course! A backwards signal... cancels out the forwards one!
That's why the second pulse didn't knock you out. The Choir was singing against it!
The Choir PROTECTED us!
The Choir hums gently above the river. Decoder, do you trust the Choir? Say yes, or no.
Do you trust the Choir? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Do you trust the Choir? Say yes, or no.
Okay. Okay. I... trust you, giant glowing alien.
Me neither! But... it did save us. Twice.
The Choir sings three notes... and then falls silent. Waiting.
It wants us to answer! We have to sing its notes back!
Decoder, the Choir sang three notes.
Sing them back! Say high, or low, for each note.
The Choir sang three notes. Say high or low for each one.
Almost! Listen to each note.
The first two notes are both high. What's the last one?
The Choir sang three notes. Say high or low for each one.
Listen again.
Say high or low for each of the three notes.
The Choir sang three notes. Say high or low for each one.
High... high... low! High, high, low!
The Choir glows brighter than ever, and its song fills the sky.
Not alone.
Never alone.
Citizens of London. Good evening. Tonight is New Year's Eve.
At the stroke of midnight, Halcyon will switch the Lattice back on... from the great wheel by the river.
A new beginning. A quiet one.
The great wheel... the London Eye. It's not just a big wheel. It's a giant transmitter!
He's going to pulse the whole city again. At midnight!
Not if the Decoders get there first.
The race to save London has begun.
End of chapter four.
Alien Invasion. Signal Decoders.
Chapter five. The Last Note.
Previously... the Decoders met the Choir, and learned the truth. The Choir protected London. Director Sterling made the pulse.
Now it's New Year's Eve. And at midnight, Sterling will pulse the whole city again... from the London Eye.
Eleven forty-five. Fifteen minutes to midnight.
Come on, come on!
The Eye's control cabin is right by the river. If I can plug my antenna into the transmitter, we can send the Choir's backwards song to the whole city!
And if we can't?
Then at midnight... London goes quiet. For good.
Great. No pressure.
They burst out onto the riverside. Above them, the London Eye towers into the dark, its centre glowing red.
Drones! Two of them, guarding the cabin!
Decoder, should they wait for the drones to fly to the other side, before they run for the cabin? Say yes, or no.
Should they wait for the drones to turn away? Say yes, or no.
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Should they wait for the drones to turn away? Say yes, or no.
They wait... and wait... The drones turn away.
Now!
No time to wait! GO!
They sprint across the snow. A drone spins round... but too late!
They tumble into the control cabin. Screens glow red, and a countdown blinks: eleven fifty-five.
Antenna in! Okay, okay. To set the counter-song, the machine needs to know how many notes are in it.
Four, two, two, one, one... the code from the very beginning!
Decoder, the code is four, two, two, one, one.
How many notes is that, altogether? Add them up, and say the number.
Four plus two plus two plus one plus one. How many notes is that, altogether?
Let's count together. Four, plus two, is six. Plus two more is...
Keep going! Add the one, and the other one. How many altogether?
Four plus two plus two plus one plus one. How many notes is that, altogether?
Four, plus two, plus two, plus one, plus one. How many notes is that, altogether?
Four plus two plus two plus one plus one. How many notes is that, altogether?
Four plus two is six. Plus two is eight. Plus one is nine. Plus one is TEN! Ten notes!
Ten! Setting it to ten... and... it's ready!
Well, well. Children. In my control cabin.
Step away from my wheel.
No way! We know all about Project Hush!
Nobody will believe you. Nobody can even hear you.
They will in a minute.
Across the river, Big Ben begins to chime midnight.
Too late. When the last bell rings, London goes quiet.
Decoder, this is it. Will you help the Decoders broadcast the truth to all of London? Say yes!
Will you help broadcast the truth to all of London? Say yes!
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Will you help broadcast the truth to all of London? Say yes!
We can't do this without you, Decoder! Please... say yes!
Will you help them broadcast the truth? Say yes!
Sorry, Decoder, the signal's a bit fuzzy. Can you say that again?
Will you help them broadcast the truth? Say yes!
Broadcasting... NOW!
From the top of the London Eye, the Choir's backwards song pours out over the city.
And then, Ada plays one more recording.
Project Hush. On Christmas night, the Lattice will sing a single note... and we'll tell them it was the sky.
Every radio in London hears it. Every survivor, in every tunnel.
No! No, no, no! Switch that off!
The last bell rings out. Twelve o'clock.
And all across London... the lights come back on.
Out of the tunnels and stations, the people of London climb up into the new year, cheering.
Not alone.
Never alone.
I'm not crying. It's the fireworks. They're very... smoky.
Happy New Year, Decoders.
So the signal was never a threat. It was a friend, trying to help... and a team of Decoders, brave enough to listen.
And Director Sterling? He was last seen running across Tower Bridge... chased by a very cross crowd, and one small Halcyon drone with a mind of its own.
The end... of season one.
